name: June Calloway
bio: June learned the guitar from her dad's tapes, mostly a single cassette from a 1977 show that she wore through twice. She started the band in 2014 with Theo after a Monday-night jam at the Lantern Room went three hours over.
gear: A 1979 hollow-body with a lot of miles on it, a Fender Twin, and a pedalboard she swears is "basically just a wah".

name: Theo Marchetti
bio: Theo sings most of the cowboy songs and all of the ones about trains. By day he restores old pianos, which is why he tunes everyone else's instrument at soundcheck.
gear: A modified semi-hollow guitar, a vintage amp head and a capo he has owned since high school.

name: Rosa Velásquez
bio: Rosa trained as a jazz pianist and joined after sitting in for one night in 2017. She brings the Rhodes, the organ and most of the strange chords. She also runs our setlist archive.
gear: A Rhodes Mark I, a clonewheel organ through a rotating speaker, and a small synth for Space.

name: Desmond Okafor
bio: Dez plays bass like a lead instrument, which is the only way to play this music. He teaches middle-school band, and some of his students now come to the all-ages shows.
gear: A six-string bass with a lot of low end, and a stack of amps the venues complain about.

name: Wren Halloran
bio: Wren keeps the band moving through the long jams and decides when a song is really over. She has played every Lantern Ramblers show since the first one.
gear: A vintage kit in champagne sparkle, with a very large ride cymbal.

name: Silas Petrakis
bio: Two drummers is part of the sound. Silas plays congas, timbales, a talking drum and, during Drums, almost anything within reach. He built the band's gong stand himself.
gear: Congas, timbales, a talking drum, and one gong.
